instruction.text: Who's talking? Listen and choose the correct person.

atoms.a: I'm originally from Australia but I moved to New Zealand for my studies when I was twenty years old. I have specialized in the medical field and now, 8 years later, I work in a clinic that specialises in the treatment of migraines, which is one of the most common neurological diseases.

instruction.text: Who's talking? Listen and choose the correct person.

atoms.a: I spend most of my day asking questions and waiting for answers… sometimes longer than you would expect. You learn quite quickly who’s prepared and who’s just hoping not to be noticed. It can be challenging, but I like seeing students improve over time. That moment when something finally clicks—it’s the best part of my job.

instruction.text: Who's talking? Listen and choose the correct person.

atoms.a: You meet all kinds of people doing this job. Some want to talk the whole time, others don’t say a word. I don’t mind either way—I’m used to both. You also get to know the city really well, especially the busy areas and the shortcuts. It can be stressful in traffic, but every day is a bit different, which I like.

instruction.text: Who's talking? Listen and choose the correct person.

atoms.a: Some days are fast-paced, and I barely have time to think before I need to act. My colleagues and I are always on the move and are confronted with various types of emergencies. Remaining calm under pressure is essential, and it feels rewarding when my decisions help someone and sometimes even save a life.
